There's a race between mm->owner assignment and swapoff
seen when task slab poisoning is turned on.  The condition occurs when
try_to_unuse() runs in parallel with an exiting task.  A similar race
can occur with callers of get_task_mm()
no other task has task->mm = task0->mm)
The fix is to notify the subsystem via mm_owner_changed callback()
if no new owner is found
column2: by specifying the new task as NULL.

column1: mm->owner was set to NULL prior to calling cgroup_mm_owner_callbacks()

column2: so as not to pass NULL as old owner causing oops.

column1: mm_update_next_owner() may set mm->owner to NULL
and its callers need to take account of this situation to avoid oops.
Lockdep warning and hang below exec_mmap() when testing these patches.
exit_mm() up_reads mmap_sem before calling mm_update_next_owner()
so exec_mmap() now needs to do the same.  And with that repositioning
there's now no point in mm_need_new_owner() allowing for NULL mm.
